title: How Does Your Phone Charge With No Cable? 🔋
description: Wireless charging runs on magnetism! Meet the two copper coils hidden in your charger and your phone — and why wireless charging makes your phone warmer.

scenes.say: You set your phone on the pad and it starts charging with no cable at all. So how does power travel through the air?
Inside the charger is a coil of copper wire, and inside your phone is another coil just like it.
The charger sends a current that flips direction very fast, creating a changing magnetic field. That field produces an electric current in the phone's coil, and the battery charges.

scenes.text: The two coils must line up exactly
scenes.say: That's why you have to place your phone in just the right spot. If the coils drift apart, charging slows down or stops.

left.label: Wireless charging
left.sub: Easier but loses energy as heat

scenes.say: Some energy is lost as heat, so wireless charging is usually slower and makes your phone warmer than charging with a cable.
